text:
lina-partnerships: Heads up — OpenCore Labs just dropped their model bundle for onboarding. License text says 'OpenAL-2.0 + territory addendum'. They explicitly call out 'restricted territories' but don’t enumerate them. Can legal confirm what we need to gate before we list it in the marketplace?

michael-legal: We need the addendum scanned for export-control language. If it’s vague, ask for a jurisdiction list and a signed attestation re: dataset provenance. Also check whether sublicensing/resale is allowed — many open licenses are fine, but the addendum can carve out redistribution rights.

tom-engineering: From infra side, we’ll need a packaging decision: do we publish an OCI image for Hosted and a tarball+checksum for Private/Dedicated? If geoblock is required, we need a flag in the SKU to disable serving in certain regions.

sara-ops: Agreed. Ops needs: 1) explicit list of blocked countries, 2) preferred distribution format, 3) any time-based embargo. Also need to know if customers can self-host the weights or if only Redwood can serve them.

aj-sales: OpenCore mentioned they want marketplace discovery but are worried about gov customers in EU/UK having stricter rules. If we have to geo-fence for CN/RU, we should surface that clearly in the listing so resellers don’t accidentally offer it.

eva-product: Product needs a model card + provenance statement. Can we ask OpenCore for: commit hashes, training data provenance summary, and a short security/privacy checklist? We’ll publish a note like 'Not for sale in: ...' if needed.

michael-legal: Draft ask for OpenCore: 1) jurisdiction list or explicit "no redistribution" clause, 2) provenance attestation, 3) CI/CD signing key/thumbprint they will use for releases, 4) indemnity clause for third-party content. Sample clause to request: "Provider shall not grant sublicenses or permit redistribution of model weights outside the territories enumerated in Exhibit A."

lina-partnerships: Good. Also confirm whether dual-licensing is possible — some providers allow 'research use' broadly but restrict commercial rehosting. If they agree to 'hosting-only' terms for marketplace, that might be acceptable.

tom-engineering: Implementation note for engineers: if hosting-only, we should add a runtime enforcement flag: `serve.allow_redistribution = false` and log attempts (audit). Can add simple check in the runtime: `if request.export_package: deny()`

sara-ops: Ops will need an SLA addendum for model updates (pulling new weights), and a purge policy if provider requests takedown. Add to checklist: 'update cadence, takedown procedure, notification window'.

aj-sales: Quick commercial ask — if OpenCore wants to bundle with hardware partners, we need to map SKU variants (hosted-only vs bundle-with-hw vs downloadable). Hardware partners often require redistribution rights for firmware-level integration, so that may be a blocker.

eva-product: For discovery UX: we should display an explicit badge: "Restricted Distribution" and list restricted regions / allowed deploy modes (Hosted, Dedicated, Private). That reduces support tickets.

michael-legal: Also watch export control lists — if weights were trained on restricted datasets or include controlled tech, we may need an export classification. Ask: was any training done with data subject to EAR/ITAR restrictions?

lina-partnerships: Action items: legal to request the four items from OpenCore (jurisdiction list, provenance attestation, signing key, indemnity); engineering to prototype the runtime flag + packaging options; ops to draft SLA + takedown steps; product to prep model card template + UX badge. I’ll ping OpenCore tonight.

deploy-bot: Created GH issue #742: "OpenCore onboarding — legal + packaging + geo-blocking" and linked PR template https://github.com/redwood/integrations/issues/742

sara-ops: Noted. Will prepare draft takedown flow (includes 48h acknowledgement window and 7-day removal target) and SKU mapping for marketplace.

tom-engineering: I’ll spike packaging today. ETA for prototype: 2 business days. Will include: OCI image + signed manifests + tarball with sha256 sums.

michael-legal: I’ll send the formal ask to OpenCore and propose an addendum template that restricts sublicensing and requires provenance attestation. If they push back on 'hosting-only', we can negotiate a limited reseller carve-out for certified hardware partners.

lina-partnerships: Thanks — if legal needs a commercial fallback, sales can propose 'certified-hardware-only redistribution' with different revenue split.

eva-product: Once we have provider responses, I’ll draft the listing UX and the model card. Include an explicit 'serving modes allowed' section.

lina-partnerships: Perfect. Thanks everyone. I’ll update thread after OpenCore replies. :thumbsup:
